children.label: c
children.prompt: By using the angle sum of a triangle, decide if $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle XYZ$ are similar.

answer.short: Yes. Both triangles have angles $40^\circ$, $55^\circ$ and $85^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\triangle PQR$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle QPR&=180^\circ-40^\circ-55^\circ\\&=85^\circ\end{align*}$$
$\triangle XYZ$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle XZY&=180^\circ-85^\circ-40^\circ\\&=55^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both triangles have angles $40^\circ$, $55^\circ$ and $85^\circ$. At least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal, so the triangles are similar (AAA).

classification.difficultyReason: Two exterior-angle steps and two third-angle calculations, then a comparison. This is scaffolded by parts and uses a routine angle sum.
Two linked angle facts: straight line, then angle sum. This is routine and single-route.

content.prompt:
For each set of three triangles, choose the two that are similar.
Choose the appropriate test and write a similarity statement (e.g. $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle FGH$).

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE$ by SSS: all three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio.
answer.worked:
Side lengths in order: $ABC$: $6,9,12$; $DEF$: $4,6,8$; $GHI$: $4,6,9$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{AB}{DF}&=\frac64=\frac32\\\frac{BC}{FE}&=\frac96=\frac32\\\frac{AC}{DE}&=\frac{12}{8}=\frac32\end{align*}$$
For $GHI$: $\frac64=\frac32$ but $\frac{12}{9}=\frac43$, so it is not similar to $ABC$.
Three pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle DFE$ by SSS.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GIH$ by SAS: two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$\angle A=\angle G=40^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{GI}{AB}&=\frac{4.5}{6}=\frac34\\\frac{GH}{AC}&=\frac{6}{8}=\frac34\end{align*}$$
Two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same ratio and the included angles are equal, so $\triangle ABC\sim\triangle GIH$ by SAS.
For $DEF$: $\frac96=\frac{12}{8}=\frac32$, but $\angle D=55^\circ\neq40^\circ$, so it is not similar to $ABC$.

classification.difficultyReason: Students choose a similar pair from three triangles and name the test. Part a needs sorted-side SSS matching. Part b needs cross-matching of the sides around 40° with a distractor triangle (DEF has the same side ratio but a 55° angle). The correspondence must be written in the right vertex order. This is about the level of p8-q9, a little harder because the correspondences are not signposted. It stays in the routine linked-procedure band.
